headline_marked: Sylhet court [[sentences ex-SI Akbar to death]] for custodial torture of Raihan Ahmed
headline: Sylhet court sentences ex-SI Akbar to death for custodial torture of Raihan Ahmed
summary: A former police sub-inspector has been sentenced to death for torturing Raihan Ahmed to death in a Sylhet police outpost. Two others received life sentences, and three received seven-year terms.
details: A Sylhet court has handed down a death sentence to dismissed police sub-inspector Akbar Hossain Bhuiyan, the main accused in the murder of Raihan Ahmed. Raihan was tortured to death at the Bandarbazar Police Outpost in Sylhet city.

The verdict was delivered on Thursday by Judge Abdul Majid Munshi of the Sylhet Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court. In addition to Akbar's death sentence, the court also sentenced two other suspects to life imprisonment and three more to seven years in prison.

Raihan Ahmed, a resident of Akhalia in Sylhet, died on October 11, 2020, after being allegedly tortured at the Bandarbazar Police Outpost. His family claimed he was taken to the outpost on suspicion of theft and subjected to severe brutality.

Following public outcry and a formal investigation, Akbar Hossain Bhuiyan, the then-sub-inspector of the outpost, was identified as the prime suspect. He was arrested and later confessed to the torture, implicating other officers.

headline_marked: UN to [[decide on Bangladesh’s LDC graduation deferment]] tonight
headline: UN to decide on Bangladesh’s LDC graduation deferment tonight
summary: The UN General Assembly will determine if Bangladesh gets a three-year extension to its preparatory period for graduating from the least developed country category.
details: The UN General Assembly is set to decide tonight whether to grant Bangladesh a three-year extension of its preparatory periods for graduation from the least developed country (LDC) category.
A senior Ministry of Finance official confirmed that Bangladesh's request to defer graduation, alongside Nepal's, is on the agenda for today's session in New York.
The session is scheduled to begin at 8pm Bangladesh time, though the exact timing of the decision has not been confirmed. A final decision requires consensus among all member states.

The government has requested an extension of the preparatory period until November 24, 2029. This follows positive recommendations from the Committee for Development Policy and the Economic and Social Council.
Bangladesh has cited several global and domestic challenges as reasons for the deferment, including volatility in global trade, geopolitical tensions, and inflationary pressures.
Additional factors include the recent crisis in the Middle East, uncertainties over global energy supplies, and changes in the international trading environment affecting the country's readiness.
caption:

The session is scheduled to begin at 8pm Bangladesh time, though the exact timing of the decision has not been confirmed. A final decision requires consensus among all member states.

The government has requested an extension of the preparatory period until November 24, 2029. This follows positive recommendations from the Committee for Development Policy and the Economic and Social Council.

Bangladesh has cited several global and domestic challenges as reasons for the deferment, including volatility in global trade, geopolitical tensions, and inflationary pressures.
